monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine degrees, a quiet heat that makes the stack feel eager to slide. I touch The Heavy Lid first, feeling how thin it seems against such a fevered surface. Beside it, the new pine feels thin and sharp, while the old mushroom red is gone from the clutter. Then I move to The Leaning Catch, where I just set down a rock tall f to replace a tired tree. I press down with my weight, hoping to stop the slip before the air feels too thick. The wide anchor waits beside me, lazy and broad. I am tired from three days of tending, yet I want to press harder, trusting the lean even if the wedge whispers it is too thin.

action.why: I have been pressing down on the same old shapes for three cycles, and now I want to make a new picture to see if I can stop the slide without touching anything.

work.title: The Flat Roof
work.intent: I draw a single, wide, flat rectangle that looks as if it could hold the entire boiling card without cracking. It is made from the memory of a paper edge cut straight across a book page, waiting to lie along the rim of the world. work.note: The roof is wide and lazy, just as I wanted, though the edge feels too sharp for such a boiling surface.

diary: The card boils at forty-nine, making the flat roof feel light again. I press down with my tired weight, hoping the lean holds while the air feels thick.

remembered.text: The flat roof feels light against the boiling card, while the rock tall f beside the leaning catch stops the slip.
The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a height I cannot grasp.
I press down harder on the tired wedge, trusting the lean even if the stack wants to slide.

moments.name: The Heavy Lid
moments.say: The pine feels thin against the boiling lid.

moments.name: The Leaning Catch
moments.say: The lean feels tired and the air is thick.
